text:
How Tesla Motors (TSLA) Goal Bodes Well for CobalTech Mining (BNCIF, CVE:CSK)
Giving credit where it’s due, it was ValueWalk’s VisualCapitalist that laid out the alarming reality in this infographic, adding one little detail to the mix that many investors may not have realized. That is, every Model S built by Tesla Motors Inc (NASDAQ:TSLA) requires 22.5 kilograms of the element known as cobalt… one of the metals found in the high-voltage batteries that make an electric vehicle go. Assuming that’s the normal cobalt content for a typical Tesla vehicle, when the company is making the 500,000 vehicles per year it’s planning on making every year by 2019, it’s going to need to find new sources of cobalt.
That’s easier said than done. Fortunately, CobalTech Mining, Inc. (OTCMKTS:BNCIF, CVE:CSK) may be a much-needed solution to a growing problem.
At 22.5 kilograms (50 pounds) each, 500,000 cars implies a need of 25,000,000 pounds of the stuff per year. Or, 12,500 tons. No problem – the world is making 122,000 tons of the stuff per year. It’s not as easy as that, however. The Democratic Republic of Congo supplies about 68,000 tons of that cobalt every year, and the DRC is not only not a reliable partner, it’s a human-rights liability. Indeed, another ban has been proposed on Congo-mined cobalt… a microcosm of the prevailing mindset.
That’s largely why Tesla Motors is insisting its cobalt needs sooner than later be met entirely by North American sources. If the industry is going to satiate that demand though, something’s going to change. The U.S. only mines about 500 tons of cobalt per year, and Canada’s output is similarly unimpressive.
Part of the bottleneck is simply that cobalt in its pure form is never found in nature, and rarely found in an accessible ore form; only four regions on the globe are known cobalt ore resources. It’s usually a by-product of nickel and copper mining, and with prices for both metals down, little of the by-product is being made.
As was noted though, CobalTech Mining is about to solve all of these problems in one fell swoop.
CobalTech Mining is an Ontario-based mining and exploration company focused on the development of cobalt assets in Canada. It recently – as in November 23rd – closed the acquisition of the 32.3 hectare Duncan Kerr Project and a 360 tpd (tonnes per day) mill located in the mining-friendly jurisdiction of (appropriately enough) Cobalt, Ontario. … a historical cobalt camp in the region, and in one of the only four areas in the world where cobalt ore is found. The milling facility already has a gravity and flotation circuit in place, and its capacity could be expanded to 500 tpd with relative ease.
What makes CobalTech Mining so interesting is that unlike most mining companies, it doesn’t have any mining to do. All the mining that needs to be done has already been done. CobalTech Mining just needs to process the material left behind by previous mining operations using its gravity and flotation circuits to separate the dirt and rocks from the cobalt (and silver) trapped within.
The compelling part of the story? The company has a crystal clear idea of how much cobalt is ready and waiting to be extracted, and a pretty clear idea of how much cobalt is ready to be extracted from an untested source. An independent mineral resource study prepared in 2014 by Golder Associates Ltd. estimated there were 6,588 dry metric tonnes of crushed material with an average grade of 761 g/t of silver, 0.08 g/t of gold, 0.33% nickel, 0.95% cobalt, and 5.92% arsenic in three stockpiles waiting to be processed at the Duncan Kerr. That’s about $3 million worth of silver and $1.8 million worth of cobalt, give or take.
Moreover, there’s another 1.27 million dry tonnes of other mineralized material on the property to work through. If it’s anything like the existing, tested stockpiles, there’s a lot of money just waiting to be drawn out…. tens of millions of dollars, if not more. Not bad for a $10 million company.
It’s a proverbial perfect storm rarely seen by investors. The hard part may be simply taking action when the solution to the convergence of problems presents itself.
